intro: One bowl of cendol has an estimated 350 kcal. Most of the calories come from santan and gula melaka.
diet: Yes, but think of cendol as a treat, not a daily drink. 350 kcal is about the same as a small meal. If you want it, pick a day when your other meals are lighter. Once or twice a week is still okay if your daily calories are under control.
tips: Ask for 'gula melaka sikit' or 'kurang manis' when you order.
Share one bowl between two. Still satisfying.
Let cendol be your sweet drink for that meal. Don't add teh tarik too.

swap.name: Cendol shared between two, less sweet
swap.why: Same taste, but half the sugar and santan. Saves over 200 kcal.

faq.a: The green cendol is made from rice flour or hun kwe flour with pandan. It's served with santan, gula melaka and shaved ice.
The natural green comes from pandan leaves. Some stalls use food colouring.

faq.q: When is the best time to eat cendol?
faq.a: Best on a hot afternoon. Avoid it late at night because it's high in sugar.
